title: The receipt printer
story:
The pizzeria's receipt printer is broken, and the night manager wants a script that prints each order's numbers. Prices and order sizes change every night, so nothing can be worked out by hand: the script has to calculate everything from three numbers at the top.

The checker will swap in different numbers and make sure your receipt still adds up.
create: The script's first three lines declare `pizzas`, `pricePerPizza` and `tip`, each in the form `local pizzas = 3` with a whole number. Use any numbers you like.

requirements.text: It declares `pizzas`, `pricePerPizza` and `tip`, each as `local name = wholeNumber`.
It prints a line exactly like `Total: 41`, where the total is pizzas times the price per pizza, plus the tip.
It prints `Big order: true` when there are 5 or more pizzas, and `Big order: false` otherwise.
It prints `Per pizza: 13`, the total divided by the number of pizzas, rounded down to a whole number.
It stores the total in a variable named `total`.

hints: Work out the total first and keep it in a variable, then build each printed line from your variables.
A comparison like greater-or-equal already gives `true` or `false`, so you can print it directly. Remember that print puts a space between the things you give it.
Rounding down while dividing is exactly what one of the operators from the maths lesson does.

static.fail: Create a Script named `Receipt` inside the `Test02` folder.
Keep the total in a variable created with `local total`.

check:
local path = "ServerScriptService.Course.Test02.Receipt"
local source = Course.source(path) or ""
local names = { "pizzas", "pricePerPizza", "tip" }
local declared = true
for _, name in names do
	if not string.find(source, "local%s+" .. name .. "%s*=%s*%d+") then
		declared = false
		Course.fail("r2", "Couldn't find a line like `local " .. name .. " = 3` with a whole number. Write it exactly in that form.")
	end
end
if declared then
	Course.pass("r2")
end

local function scenario(pizzas, price, tip)
	local replace = {
		{ "local%s+pizzas%s*=%s*%d+", "local pizzas = " .. pizzas },
		{ "local%s+pricePerPizza%s*=%s*%d+", "local pricePerPizza = " .. price },
		{ "local%s+tip%s*=%s*%d+", "local tip = " .. tip },
	}
	return Course.run(path, { replace = replace })
end

local function has(prints, wanted)
	for _, line in prints do
		if line == wanted then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

local first = Course.run(path)
Course.check("r3", first.ok, "Your script stopped with an error: " .. tostring(first.error))

if declared then
	for _, case in { { 3, 12, 5 }, { 6, 10, 7 }, { 5, 9, 0 }, { 1, 4, 2 } } do
		local pizzas, price, tip = case[1], case[2], case[3]
		local run = scenario(pizzas, price, tip)
		local setup = string.format("With pizzas = %d, pricePerPizza = %d and tip = %d", pizzas, price, tip)
		if not run.ok then
			Course.fail("r3", setup .. ", your script errored: " .. tostring(run.error))
		end
		local total = pizzas * price + tip
		Course.check("r4", has(run.prints, "Total: " .. total),
			setup .. ", expected a line `Total: " .. total .. "`. Your script printed " .. Course.show(run.prints))
		local big = if pizzas >= 5 then "true" else "false"
		Course.check("r5", has(run.prints, "Big order: " .. big),
			setup .. ", expected a line `Big order: " .. big .. "`. Your script printed " .. Course.show(run.prints))
		local each = total // pizzas
		Course.check("r6", has(run.prints, "Per pizza: " .. each),
			setup .. ", expected a line `Per pizza: " .. each .. "`. Your script printed " .. Course.show(run.prints))
	end
else
	for _, id in { "r4", "r5", "r6" } do
		Course.fail(id, "Not checked yet: the three starting lines need to be in the exact form shown, so the checker can try other numbers.")
	end
end
steps: Make the first three lines `local pizzas = 3`, `local pricePerPizza = 12` and `local tip = 5`. You can pick any whole numbers.
Make a variable called `total`: pizzas times pricePerPizza, plus tip.
Print a line that reads `Total: ` followed by the total.
Print `Big order: true` when pizzas is 5 or more, otherwise `Big order: false`.
Print `Per pizza: ` followed by the total divided by pizzas, rounded down. The `//` operator divides and rounds down in one go.
Don't type any answers yourself: the checker swaps in other numbers and expects every line to change to match.
example:
With pizzas = 3, pricePerPizza = 12 and tip = 5:
Total: 41
Big order: false
Per pizza: 13
